name: villains
description: The ones the story is against. Storybook villains in torn paper, drawn with more edge and expression than the rest of the cast — cloaks, crooked stances, faces that are up to something. Twelve pieces, from two sheets; the second sheet is a little sharper and more angular than the first.
stylePrompt:
STYLE — follow this exactly, it matters more than the subject: Torn and cut paper collage. Every single shape is a piece of coloured paper that has been cut with scissors or torn by hand and laid flat on top of the others, with visible torn deckle edges, paper grain, fibre and a dry speckled gouache texture inside each shape. Small details — faces, eyes, buckles, stitching — are drawn on top in fine black ink line. Seen STRAIGHT ON, flat, from the front — the way an audience sees a puppet theatre or a paper cut-out stage. There is no vanishing point and no perspective anywhere. Depth is made only by putting one flat shape in front of another, never by making things smaller as they go back. ABSOLUTELY NOT: digital painting, watercolour, gouache painting, concept art, rendered 3D, airbrushing, photorealism, cinematic lighting, volumetric light, glow, ambient occlusion, depth of field, blur, gradients, soft shading, cast shadows, reflections, perspective depth, or texture that looks painted rather than papery. Nothing is lit. Nothing is round. Nothing recedes. Everything is flat. Shapes are simple, geometric and slightly naive — built from a few pieces, the way a child's paper cut-out is. Palette: muted, warm and mid-century — moss and olive green, deep navy used instead of black, brick red, cream, dusty rose, mustard, soft pink. Four to six colours in total, used as large flat areas.

The sheet is a cast of storybook villains — one per cell, all different: the kind a children's play is against. Give each one a readable silhouette and a stance that says what they are before the audience hears a word.

Draw ONE sheet: a 5 × 5 grid of 25 separate pictures. Each cell is 1:1 — square. The cells must be exactly equal in size and evenly spaced, filling the whole image edge to edge, in reading order. Leave a clear even gap between cells and keep every subject well inside its own cell — nothing may touch or cross a cell edge. No grid lines, no borders, no numbers, no captions, no text, no watermark. NO WHITE OUTLINES. Do not draw a white keyline, a die-cut sticker border, a stroke or a glow around anything. This is not a sticker pack. NO OUTLINES. Before you draw anything, write out all 25 descriptions and check them: every one must be a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT character, not a variation of its neighbour. 25 genuinely different things, or the sheet is wasted.

Each cell holds ONE character on a PLAIN WHITE background, cut-out style, with no shadow, no ground, no scenery and no base beneath them. Full body, facing the viewer, standing upright with their feet visible and their arms clear of their sides — they will be animated walking, jumping and bowing, so nothing may be cropped and nothing may merge into the background. Keep the same scale, the same lighting and the same level of detail across every cell.

Then cut it up at https://fastcut.needle.tools: fastcut_add_image, fastcut_set_output_format (WebP), fastcut_split_sprites, fastcut_download as a ZIP.

witch.description: a hook-nosed witch in a pointed hat, leaning on a broom — the tallest villain, and the one a child recognises fastest

vampire.description: a vampire with his cloak spread wide — the widest silhouette in the pack, so give him room

evil-queen.description: a crowned queen with a high collar, fingers steepled — cold rather than loud

pirate.description: a pirate captain with an eyepatch and a hook, feet planted apart — the most comic of the six

mad-scientist.description: a wild-haired scientist in a pink coat, fingers steepled, glasses flashing

masked-thief.description: a masked thief crouched mid-creep, arms out — already in a pose, so he reads as sneaking even standing still

warlord.description: an armoured warlord with a red crest, fists on hips — the bulkiest villain, built to loom

sorceress.description: a white-haired sorceress in a pale gown with a spiked collar, arms raised mid-spell

jester.description: a jester in mustard and pink diamonds, caught mid-caper — a villain who is funny until he is not

highwayman.description: a caped figure under a wide hat, leaning on a cane — waiting rather than attacking

gentleman-schemer.description: a gaunt man in a top hat and green suit, fingertips together — the polite kind of villain

creeping-fiend.description: a wild-haired figure crouched low with clawed hands — already creeping, so he reads as up to something standing still
